main_text.p: espectu habito ad superiorem suam [?]entiam & Praxin, vel ad rem & existimationem totius Cleri communem, pretâ Ordinis, Doctrinæ, & Religionis curâ, contra omnia denique Veterum Ecclesiarum exempla, Leges Regni constitutas, & confensu mMeum, qui cernere nunquam impetrabit adversus [?]am illam lucem, quâ Intellectus meus in hoc Articulo illustratur.

In rebus enim ejusmodi, quæ non [?]erindè ex professo rationi aut Fidei aut Bonis Moribus adversantur, & circa quæ in Scriptura haud ita clarè & distinctè præcipitur, ibi certe perpetua & universalis Praxis Ecclesiæ optima est quam sequamur Regula.

Quod ad me attinet, promptus eram vel donare Presbyteratui vel restituere, quicquid Episcopatui conjunctus intra Rationis & Prudentiæ terminos postulasset: ut vero ita penitus invadat illam Potestatem, & Gladio afferat, & Antiqui illius Ordinis Jura aboleat, id nec justum in Episcopatum nec Presbyteratui tutum existimo, nec ullo modo vel Ecclesiæ vel Reipublicæ convenire.
Moderata certe consilia haud difficulter secuta fuisset debita Reformatio; atque ea forsan quæ longè gratior fuisset iis Ipsis Theologis, qui ipsi prius decepti

page.notes: Left-edge clipping: the first letter of "sententiam" (line 1) and of "clam" (line 5) and the first letter of "perindè" (line 6) are cut off by the scan edge; the reading is inferred from context, so these words are marked [?]. The "m" before "Meum" (line 4) is printed as roman m directly before italic Meum; kept as printed. "Reformatio;" ends with a mark read as a semicolon; uncertain. The running head Greek is copied as printed. The page number reads 133 (printed in old-style figures). Stray marks at the very foot of the page (dots) are not printed text and were left out.
